Messages.Author: Wes
Messages.Body:
"salem" <salem_ch...@yahoo.com> wrote

> so...from the WoD, what are the Holds from anarchs supposed to
> represent? Places? Powers? Kung-Fu moves?

Michaelis was the Ventrue Justicar that Kemintiri killed and then
impersonated for a while. You can see how popular that made her by reading
Kemintiri's card text :)

Not sure who Cold Amber, Chiram or Regarhagan are. I'm assuming they are
also meant to represent the influences of very old vampires ie "Methuselahs"

Maybe whoever designed them can speak out? (Doubt it)

> also....what do people think of them, vtes wise? which are the 'best',
> what kind of deck would you put each one in?

I haven't used any yet.

They don't seem that great to me. I like the idea of hosing someone else's
most commonly used cards, but it doesn't cost them much to get around the
bad effects. Look at Chiram's Hold. First you need to wait for them to
discard a Majesty. Then you need to block one of the Majesty-cheese-users
vampires. Even then all it does is make them pay an extra blood... woohoo.
And to add insult to your own injuries, all they need do is discard *one
Majesty* and the card is gone. I imagine *you* will probably spend more
precious resources on this card than they will.

They also seem to have higher opportunity costs than most cards... and you
*know* that you will draw it at exactly the wrong time.

Oh well, the idea certainly has potential.

> I have chiram's hold in a gangrel/ravnos combat deck, due to my lack
> of ability to deal with 'combat ends' through other means (only own
> one dog pack). do people think chiram's is best offensively or
> defensively? or is it's flexibility what's best about it?

You have to block them to use it so I would imagine it is better as
defensive.

You're better off not worrying about combat ends and just focus on being
persistent. Eventually they will run out. We hope.

Cheers,
WES

Hmmm... Chiram's hold actually looks the best of the bunch, since
there is little oppertunity cost wasted in getting it into play... if
you use the right sort of deck. Since you can get it into play before
range in any combat and it only costs a blood (not pool like some of
them!) you can use it pretty easily in a combat deck. I instantly
thought of two clans that could benefit from it:

1) Assamites. Combine with Thin Blood and Wave of Lethargy to nuke 2 -
5 blood off a vampire by the time strikes are sorted. That pretty much
empties, or at least deflates, most vampires. If they can't pay, you
can hit them hard. If they can pay, Psyche (3 cards to torporise most
vampires). Trick is blocking a vampire with Assamites... not so easy.

2) Tzimisce. Actually, all Animalism combat, but mostly the Tzimisce.
Once again, the Tzimisce score a critical hit with this card in
combination with Terror Frenzy. Terror Frenzy means all combat cards
cost more, Chirams Hold means their key combat card costs even more.
You hit back for agg and watch them burn. No trouble blocking either!
It should also work with the likes of Skin Trap and Carrion Crows for
+1 pain.

Chiram's Hold could also be useful working back against other combat
decks (e.g. Potence / Celerity, Animalism, Cel Guns, etc) who are
likely to go down with a struggle - hit their key card (Blue, Immortal
Grapple, etc) and watch them sweat for the rest of the turn.

<snip>

DH

Messages.Author: Ped Xing
Messages.Body:
"Wes" <gh...@NYETSPAMmnsi.net> wrote:

> Look at Chiram's Hold. First you need to wait for them to
> discard a Majesty. Then you need to block one of the Majesty-cheese-users
> vampires. Even then all it does is make them pay an extra blood... woohoo.
> And to add insult to your own injuries, all they need do is discard *one
> Majesty* and the card is gone.

Gotta disagree here. Chirams Hold is fabulous. It does not require, as
you note, that you block, only that you are in combat, thus in any
deck with CEL it can be played after a Psyche. Also, yes they can
remove it by discarding another copy of the card, but this cannot be
done until their own discard phase, which could very easily be a turn
around the table. Furthermore, in a deck where s:ce or skin of steel
is the primary combat defense, you can't really aford to be discarding
them without playing them in combat, especially against an opponent
that's playing dedicated combat. Think of the effect that it has on a
card like Coma?

Also, in a close-range Assamite combat deck this is an amazing card,
especially when paired with Thin Blood.

-Matt

Messages.Author: The Fanboy
Messages.Body:
>but this cannot be done until their own discard phase, which could
very >easily be a turn around the table. Furthermore, in a deck where
s:ce or skin >of steel is the primary combat defense, you can't really
aford to be >discarding them without playing them in combat,
especially against an opponent
>that's playing dedicated combat. Think of the effect that it has on a
>card like Coma?

In addition, they're ditchinig combat cards that WILL be useful, and
probably necessary, for them to play, instead of anything that's
clearing up their hand jam. THat's a huge opportunity cost. You've
got two masters, both of which cost pook you can't afford, and a
Majesty. Do you ditch one of the masters that you'll never play,
upping your effective hand size by one, or do you ditch the Majesty to
get rid of the hold?

That's a touch call. The hold adds up over a few combats, especially
with Majesty and most of the other S:CE cards costing blood now to
begin with. But watching your hand size shrink as cards you'll never
play creep into your hand while at the same time getting rid of a hold
that could well be put back out by your predator or prey before your
next turn...

Fanboy
